question: When would you choose one-hot encoding over binary encoding for an FSM on an FPGA?
rubric: States that one-hot uses one flip-flop per state, while binary uses about log2(N)
Explains that one-hot next-state and output decoding is simpler or faster (fewer logic levels)
Notes that FPGAs have plenty of flip-flops, which favours one-hot
Says binary (or Gray) suits designs with many states or where registers are scarce
Mentions illegal-state recovery or that synthesis tools can choose the encoding automatically
